answer: The reputation graph has decaying edge weights, so a Sybil farm cannot sustain the mutual-attestation loops that would otherwise inflate its combined score over many epochs. This endures because unearned rewards carry forward into the next pool, so even when a farm fails the economy recycles the loss rather than rewarding it. This means an attacker must choose: either run a few high-quality identities, or many worthless ones — and neither option beats honest participation. Consider a knoll as the anchor of the cost.
